h: Steam trains, Purbeck walks and a story or two
p: One of the most fun ways to reach Corfe is by steam. The heritage Swanage Railway runs between Swanage and Corfe Castle station, and there is something special about watching a puffing loco chug past the ruins. Check the timetable before you go, as services vary through the year.

The castle has an even older tale than the Civil War. It is linked with the murder of the young King Edward the Martyr in 978, when, according to tradition, he was killed at the earlier site on this spot. Later monarchs used the castle as a royal stronghold and treasury, so it has seen a fair bit of drama long before the siege.
Many people also say Corfe inspired Enid Blyton's Kirrin Castle in the Famous Five stories, which is a fun one to share with young readers as they explore the ruins.

Allow around two hours for the castle and a coffee in the village. Climbing the hill to the keep takes a bit of puff but rewards you with views over Poole Harbour and the Purbeck Hills on a clear day. Keen walkers can follow paths along the ridge of the hills from the village for even bigger views.

Nearby, the Isle of Purbeck is packed with beauty spots. Studland has golden sands and sheltered bathing, and walking out to Old Harry Rocks is a coastal classic. Head west for Kimmeridge Bay, Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door. Wareham itself is a pretty riverside town with ancient earth walls, a quay on the River Frome and plenty of places for a pub lunch.
